masterBuilder.title: Master card
masterBuilder.name: Name
masterBuilder.name-tip: A short name, for example the chapter or topic this master covers. It is the question on the study card.
masterBuilder.status-tip: Draft: still being built. Active: in use. Archived: kept for reference. It is only a label; it does not change how the master is studied.
masterBuilder.levels-tip: These names come from your hierarchy (Settings > Hierarchy). Decks nest as the deck levels, the sections of this master are the section level, and each entry is one entry level item.
masterBuilder.empty: No sections yet. Add one to start.
masterBuilder.limit: A master holds at most {{max}} entries.
masterBuilder.bulk-tip: Each entry without a card gets the card whose text is most similar. Cards that no entry uses yet win ties. Untick any that are wrong.
masterBuilder.bulk-none: No good matches found. Link entries one by one with the link button on each row.
masterBuilder.activities-tip: Recall sweep: write down what you remember, then check yourself. Gap hunt: work through the coverage problems as a checklist. Weak-spot drill: a study session with only the weakest cards linked from this master. None of them changes a card's memory data by itself.
masterBuilder.coverage-tip: Coverage is the share of the deck's cards that some entry links to. Entries may also link to cards of other decks; those do not count here.
masterBuilder.coverage-line: {{pct}}% ({{covered}} of {{total}} cards are in an entry)
masterBuilder.orphans-tip: Cards of this deck that no entry links to. Adding them as entries makes the master complete.
masterBuilder.dangling: entries point at a missing card
masterBuilder.dangling-tip: The linked card was deleted. Unlinking keeps the entry text; an entry with no text is removed.
masterBuilder.unlinked-tip: An entry with only text is not tested by any card yet.
masterBuilder.suspended-tip: A suspended card is hidden from study, so the entry is never reviewed.
masterBuilder.needs-study: entries never reviewed or long overdue
masterBuilder.needs-study-tip: Their cards are new or more than 30 days overdue.
masterBuilder.dup-card: cards are used by several entries
masterBuilder.dup-card-tip: One card linked from more than one entry. Keeping the first removes the others.
masterBuilder.dup-text-tip: Entries that share almost all their words.
masterBuilder.gap-tip: Every gap in the coverage report is one line. Fix it with its button, or tick it when you have looked at it. Fixed gaps disappear after a moment.
masterBuilder.gap-clear: No gaps. Every card is covered and every entry has a card.
masterBuilder.sweep-tip: Type (or say) what you remember, then reveal and mark each entry found or missed. The result feeds the suggested rating. It never changes a card's memory data; moving missed cards to today is a separate button.
masterBuilder.sweep-type: What do you remember? One {{noun}} per line
masterBuilder.sweep-type-hint: Lines, commas or semicolons separate items.
masterBuilder.sweep-mark: Mark each {{noun}} you recalled. Matches are pre-ticked; check them.
masterBuilder.suggestion-only: Suggestion only. You choose the rating.
masterBuilder.sweep-bring-note: Only moves their due date to now. Their memory data stays as it is. New cards are skipped.
masterBuilder.deck-tip: A master card lists every concept of the deck with nothing left out. Open the builder to edit it, or start an activity.
masterBuilder.deck-none: No master yet. Create one with an entry for every card, then group and edit it.

learn.maximumIntervalDescription: The maximum interval in days between two repetitions of a card
learn.newToReviewRatioDescription: This determines how many new cards will be new cards will be shown per review on average. A value of 0.5 means that reviews and new cards will be ordered in equal amounts.
learn.requestRetentionDescription: Set which percentage of questions you want to be able to remember in the long-term. Note: High values will lead to more reviews and shorter intervals. Lower percentages will generally reduce the amount of learning. If requested retention is too low, you will forget your cards too often which may result in an increased learning demand. Recommended values lie between 0.70 and 0.95.
learn.schedulerWeightsDescription: FSRS calculates the next interval based on these parameters. For more information, please refer to the FSRS documentation. We may add additional documentation and tools to help you optimize these values in the future.
